newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Chevron seeks PNG gas partners.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Chevron seeks PNG gas partners.

text.p: Chevron Corp said on Friday it had issued an advance notice seeking participants for construction, ownership and operation of a A$2 billion Australian and Papua New Guinea (PNG) gas pipeline project.
Chevron subsidiary Chevron South Pacific Co is currently developing the PNG/Queensland gas project consisting of gas production and LPG extraction along with processing facilities.

"Chevron is interested in exploring the possibility of participation by an additional party or parties in one or more of its three pipeline segments - from PNG to the Australian border, the PNG border to Townsville (Australia) and from Townsville to Gladstone (Australia)," the company said.

Chevron has said it aims to begin commercial delivery of gas to markets in north Queensland and potentially central Queensland by about July 2000, drawing gas from the Kutubu and other gas field in PNG.

Offshore in the Gulf of Papua, the Pandora gas field could also be tied in to the pipeline as markets expand, Chevron has said. Chevron has already agreed to a joint effort in planning the pipeline with the partners in the Pandora field.
Pandora is located in the PPL 82 offshore permit.

The PPL 82 joint venture is headed by Canada's International Petroleum Corp (48.1890 percent), Mobil Corp unit Ampolex Ltd (16.3636 percent), the Command Petroleum Ltd subsidiary of Cairn Energy Plc (12.7273 percent), Beach Petroleum NL (6.3636) and Oil Search Ltd and Secab Mining Pty Ltd (5.0 percent each).

Kutubu participants are Chevron Niugini Pty Ltd (19.375 percent), Oil Search Ltd (7.763 percent), Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd unit BHP Petroleum (PNG) Inc (9.688 percent), BP Australia Ltd 19.375 percent), Ampolex 16.455 (percent), Mitsubishi Oil co Ltd affiliate JPP (4.844 percent) and the PNG government (22.50 percent).

Chevron estimates it operates projects with reserves of more than 13,000 petajoules for the pipeline. An initial market of between 60 and 65 petajoules a year, plus some growth is needed for the project to be viable, Chevron has said.
